# linux_sysctl (Resource)

Sets a kernel parameter now, with `sysctl -w`, and after reboots, in a file of `/etc/sysctl.d`. Destroying the resource removes the parameter from the file but leaves its current value.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_sysctl" "ip_forward" {
  name  = "net.ipv4.ip_forward"
  value = "1"
}

resource "linux_sysctl" "port_range" {
  name  = "net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range"
  value = "1024 65000"
  file  = "/etc/sysctl.d/90-network.conf"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the parameter, such as `net.ipv4.ip_forward`.
- `value` (String) Value. Fields of multi-valued parameters are separated by spaces, such as `32768 60999`.

### Optional

- `file` (String) File persisting the parameter. Defaults to `/etc/sysctl.d/99-terraform.conf`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Name of the parameter.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the name of the parameter, persisted in /etc/sysctl.d/99-terraform.conf.
terraform import linux_sysctl.ip_forward net.ipv4.ip_forward
```
